memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The elders of Moab and Midian left, taking with them the fee for divination. When they came to Balaam, they told him what Balak had said. "Spend the night here," Balaam said to them, "and I will report back to you with the answer the LORD gives me." So the Moabite officials stayed with him. God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?" - Num 22:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The messengers arrive with the fee for divination in hand, and Balaam invites them to stay the night. He says he will wait for the Lord's answer. On the surface this sounds proper, even godly. But the presence of that payment already hints that Balaam's heart may be divided.

Then God speaks. He asks Balaam a question: "Who are these men with you?" Of course God already knew. His questions are never for gathering information; they are for searching the heart. It is the same gentle probing we hear when God asked Adam, "Where are you?"

God's questions invite us to be honest about where we stand. He was giving Balaam an opportunity to examine his own motives, to consider why these men had come and what he truly desired. The fee sat there as a quiet test of Balaam's loyalty.

We face such moments too. God often knows exactly what we are doing, yet He allows a pause for us to be honest with ourselves and with Him. When your motives are mixed, do not hide behind spiritual-sounding words. Come clean before the Lord who sees the heart, and trust His grace in Christ to lead you rightly (Heb 4:13).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there mixed motives in your heart that God is inviting you to examine?
2. Do you use spiritual language to cover divided loyalties?
3. What would it mean to be fully honest with God about your desires?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see my heart completely, even the motives I try to hide. Search me and lead me in honesty, that I may follow You with an undivided heart. Amen.
